findings.title: Fix the invalid closing conditional in the embed template
findings.body: The template closes its conditional with `end if`, but the trailing `if` has no condition. ERB therefore generates invalid Ruby and raises a syntax error when rendering this view. Once an embedded topic has been retrieved, requests switch from the loading page to a server error instead of displaying the discussion.

findings.title: Preserve HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts
findings.body: Returning `raw` bypasses sanitization as well as Markdown rendering. RSS bodies reach this path after only entity decoding and a Nokogiri parse, which preserve scripts and event handlers. The importer also interpolates the attribution URL directly into HTML, so a valid article URL containing `?x='onmouseover='alert(1)` can inject an event-handler attribute even when Readability cleaned the article. This output is persisted as cooked HTML and rendered unescaped on the forum origin. Imported posts also retain this unsafe cooking mode on subsequent edits.

findings.title: Validate redirect destinations during embedded-page retrieval
findings.body: TopicRetriever checks the allowlisted host only on the original embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without rechecking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects elsewhere can therefore make the worker fetch off-allowlist or internal services, potentially importing their responses into a topic. The embed-triggered retrieval path must enforce its host restriction before following each redirect.

findings.title: Bound remotely downloaded content before parsing it
findings.body: The visitor-controlled embed URL is restricted only by host, so it can identify a large video, archive, or other asset on the allowed site rather than an article. `open(url).read` downloads and buffers the complete response, then passes it to Readability/Nokogiri without a size limit or content-type check. Such requests can exhaust the Sidekiq process's memory. Enforce a download-size limit and reject unsuitable responses before HTML parsing.

findings.title: Handle standard RSS body fields and entries without content
findings.body: Valid RSS feeds commonly put article HTML in `description` or `content:encoded`, while Atom entries may provide only `summary`. These entries do not have an `i.content` value, so calling `scrub` on it fails and aborts the entire polling run before subsequent entries are imported. Select an available body field and explicitly handle entries with no body.

findings.title: Resolve relative URLs using URI semantics
findings.body: The current rewriting turns a protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` into `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, losing the intended host. It also leaves path-relative values such as `images/photo.jpg` unchanged, so they resolve against the Discourse page instead of the source article. This breaks common imported links and images. Resolve both href and src values against the article URL rather than stripping leading slashes and concatenating a host prefix.

findings.title: Defer post-processing jobs until the outer import transaction commits
findings.body: PostCreator.create enqueues feature_topic_users and process_post after its own transaction block, but this caller wraps that block in an outer Topic.transaction. The nested transaction has not committed when those jobs are published, so separate Sidekiq workers can run before the post or topic is visible. If creating the embed subsequently fails, the jobs reference rolled-back records. Job publication needs to occur after the outermost transaction commits.

findings.title: Handle simultaneous imports of the same URL
findings.body: The existence lookup occurs before the creation transaction and does not serialize imports. The hourly feed poll and on-demand retrievals can import the same feed concurrently, allowing both callers to observe no embed and create a topic before one loses the unique embed_url insert race. The resulting RecordNotUnique exception aborts that feed's remaining entries, and scheduled polling has retries disabled. Serialize creation per URL or recover from the conflict by loading the winning embed.

findings.title: Set the retrieval throttle and its expiration atomically
findings.body: SETNX creates the throttle key without an expiration, and EXPIRE is issued separately. If EXPIRE fails or the worker exits between these commands, the article has not been retrieved but its key remains permanently present. Every later retrieval then reports it as recently retrieved, leaving the embed on the loading page indefinitely. Set the key and its TTL in one atomic operation.

findings.title: Preserve original thread timestamps during Disqus imports
findings.body: The old topic creation forwarded the Disqus thread's created_at value, but import_remote receives only its title and creates the initial post with the current time. Replies still retain their historical dates. Imported discussions therefore have a first post newer than their replies and are dated and ordered as newly created discussions rather than preserving the exported history. Forward the thread timestamp through the import helpers.

findings.title: Do not require archived Disqus source pages to remain reachable
findings.body: Importing each thread now performs a remote page fetch without exception handling. A normal 404 or connection failure for an archived permalink raises from open-uri and aborts the entire import, even though that thread's comments and all subsequent threads are already available in the XML export. Retain a permalink-only fallback when retrieving the source article fails so the comment migration can still complete.

findings.title: Update dependency locks for the other supported Rails boot modes
findings.body: The new dependencies are unconditional, but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated. This Gemfile still selects Gemfile.lock in RAILS3 mode and Gemfile_rails_master.lock in RAILS_MASTER mode. Frozen or deployment installs using those modes now have lockfiles that disagree with the Gemfile and fail dependency installation. Update the corresponding lockfiles or scope the dependencies to the supported mode.
